source.publisher: ExxonMobil crude oil assay library (assays by ExxonMobil Technology & Engineering Company)
source.method: Cut Data table of each assay's XLS (sheet 'Summary (C)'), 'Yield (% vol)' row. The seven standard cuts are groupings of the assay's temperature cuts: butane and lighter = IBP–C5 (an explicit IBP–C4 column in the 2026-format files); light naphtha = C5–100 °C; heavy naphtha = 100–150 °C; kerosene = 150–250 °C; diesel = 250–350 °C; vacuum gas oil = 350–550 °C (includes the 350–370 °C atmospheric cut); vacuum residue = 550 °C–FBP. In every file the 370 °C–FBP column is the total of the four vacuum sub-cuts (370–450, 450–500, 500–550, 550–FBP), so it is not added a second time. The reported cuts sum to 100% (99.96–100.0, rounding) for each crude, and the cumulative row's differences match the yields. Provenance per cut: 'reported' means a single column of the assay's 'Yield (% vol)' row (butane and lighter in the 2026-format files, heavy naphtha 100-150 deg C, residue 550 deg C-FBP); 'derived' means a sum of reported sub-cuts (see derived_from on each cut) or, for Kearl's butane and lighter, a residual cross-checked against the assay's TBP curve.
source.basis: Straight-run (distillation) yields, % of barrel volume. These are NOT final product yields: naphtha becomes gasoline and VGO/residue becomes other fuels only after further processing.

cuts.note: The 2023-format cut table has no gas column; the value is 100 minus the sum of the reported cuts (98.60), matching the assay's own TBP curve volume at the C5 boundary (10.58 at 65 °C minus the reported C5–65 cut of 9.18) and the table's cumulative row (0.86 % wt at C5).
